$comment: The render context for templates/display-manager/sddm.conf.j2. One required name: the SDDM display server. One optional name: the Wayland greeter compositor command, defaulted in the template because the rendered config must always name a compositor. The DM TYPE, packages, the Pixie pin and service enablement stay in the installer (spine AD-9) — only the file body is an asset.
title: display-manager/sddm.conf.j2 — render context
description: The values the SDDM config reads: DisplayServer (wayland or x11) and the optional Wayland greeter compositor command (template default: weston --shell=kiosk).

display_manager_sddm_display_server.description: SDDM's DisplayServer value. Enumerated because these are the two values the directive accepts; the consumer's default is `wayland` (the no-X11-GPU-grab choice the template documents).

display_manager_sddm_compositor_command.description: The Wayland greeter's `[Wayland] CompositorCommand`. Optional: the template defaults to `weston --shell=kiosk`, which is also SDDM's implicit default; the consumer overrides it only when it installs a different compositor. The default lives in the body, not here, so the rendered file always carries a command.

x-render-contract.no_default_on_required: No `default(` fallback on the display server: it is a login-path decision, and a silently defaulted value is exactly the kind of broken-greeter state this file cannot detect. The compositor command is different: it is optional, defaults in the body to SDDM's implicit `weston --shell=kiosk`, and `make validate-templates` asserts both the fallback and an explicit override.
x-render-contract.assets_scope: No mode, ownership, service name or package list here (spine AD-9): the installer renders this at 0644 with become and owns enablement. The compositor package (`weston` by default) and the pin to this repository stay in the consumer.
